question: The income of Raman is ₹68,500. He saves 22.5% of his income. If his income increases by 14% and expenditure increases by 40%, then his savings will:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let Income = 100 units, Savings = 22.5 units, Expenditure = 77.5 units.

Income increase = 14% of 100 = 14 units.

Expenditure increase = 40% of 77.5 = 31 units.

Savings change = 14 − 31 = −17 units (Decrease).

Given 100 units = ₹68,500 ⇒ 17 units = 17 × 685 = ₹11,645.

**∴ The correct option is C.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Income = ₹68,500, Savings Percentage = 22.5%

**Formula Used:**

Income = Expenditure + Savings

 Income: ₹68,500 (100%) Exp: 77.5% Sav: 22.5% 
• Income ↑ 14% (₹9,590) | Exp ↑ 40% (₹21,235) Savings Decrease = ₹11,645 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Original Savings = 22.5% of 68,500 = (22.5 ÷ 100) × 68,500 = ₹15,412.5

⇒ Original Expenditure = 68,500 − 15,412.5 = ₹53,087.5

⇒ Increase in Income = 14% of 68,500 = (14 ÷ 100) × 68,500 = ₹9,590

⇒ Increase in Expenditure = 40% of 53,087.5 = (40 ÷ 100) × 53,087.5 = ₹21,235

⇒ Change in Savings = Increase in Income − Increase in Expenditure

⇒ Change in Savings = 9,590 − 21,235 = −₹11,645

⇒ The negative value denotes a decrease in savings.

**∴ The correct option is C.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income-Expenditure Identity

The fundamental relation is Income = Expenditure + Savings. Any change in two components directly determines the change in the third.

Net Change in Savings

Change in Savings = (Income × Income increase %) − (Expenditure × Expenditure increase %). If the result is negative, savings have decreased.

Percentage Change Formula

Percentage change in savings = (Change in Savings ÷ Original Savings) × 100. This helps in identifying the growth or reduction rate.
